scenarios.description: Changing-capacity scale-up: cluster starts at 4 CPU and scales to 8 CPU at t=10s. scale-big (6 CPU, 18s) is infeasible on the initial 4 CPU cluster; scale-small (4 CPU, 4s) fits on the initial 4 CPU cluster. Under FIFO scale-big blocks the queue head (HOL blocking); after the scale-up event scale-big is admitted (using 6 of 8 CPU), leaving only 2 CPU free — scale-small needs 4 CPU so it cannot be admitted until scale-big finishes at t=28, then runs from t=28 to t=32 (exceeds the 30s horizon). Under greedy scale-small runs first (t=0 to t=4) before the scale-up, then scale-big runs from t=10 to t=28 — both complete within the horizon.
scenarios.name: dev_changing_capacity_scaleup

scenarios.description: FIFO head-of-line blocking: an infeasible trial at the head of the queue (requests 6 CPU on a 4-CPU cluster) blocks a feasible 2-CPU trial behind it. Under FIFO both trials stall; under greedy the infeasible head is skipped and the feasible trial runs. No cycles — this is NOT a nested-resource deadlock, just a queue policy artefact.
scenarios.name: dev_fifo_hol_blocking

scenarios.description: GPU STRICT_PACK fragmentation: two GPU trials each reserve half the GPU pool under STRICT_PACK (2 of 4 GPUs) but each nested child demands the FULL pool (4 GPUs). Each trial is admitted because its parent fits, but each child can never fit because the other parent holds the remaining GPUs. Both trials enter WAITING_CHILD and form self-cycles — two cycles total. Even greedy cannot fix this because both parents fit at admission time.
scenarios.name: dev_gpu_strict_pack_fragmentation

scenarios.description: PyTorch nested contention: a parent trial reserves only part of the cluster (2 CPU of 4) but its nested child demands more than the entire cluster (4 CPU). The parent is admitted but the child cannot fit, creating a self-cycle. The remaining 2 CPU of free capacity is enough for a concurrent small PyTorch job with no nested child, which completes normally. Proves the observer can simultaneously track a nested deadlock AND a healthy concurrent trial.
scenarios.name: dev_pytorch_nested_contention

scenarios.description: Source case: Ray issue #47439. A 4-CPU cluster; the XGBoost tuning trial reserves a 4-CPU parent placement group, then its nested distributed trainer requests a 3-CPU child placement group. The child cannot fit because the parent holds the entire cluster. The trial enters WAITING_CHILD indefinitely and forms a self-cycle in the wait-for graph.
scenarios.name: dev_ray47439_xgboost_deadlock

scenarios.description: Safe gang-scheduled jobs: two atomic gang-scheduled jobs that each reserve a placement group fitting the cluster exactly. They run sequentially without nested children, completing cleanly under both FIFO and greedy. Establishes a positive baseline that the observer does not flag false positives.
scenarios.name: dev_safe_gang_scheduled

scenarios.description: Safe control: same shape as the source case (parent + nested XGBoost child) but on a larger cluster so the child placement can be admitted without contention. Proves the observer does NOT label every nested request as a deadlock.
scenarios.name: dev_safe_nested_xgboost

scenarios.description: Acceptance fixture (hash-frozen, NOT included in CP-1 totals): node-loss recovery under CP-2. A trial enters RUNNING, then loses its resources (simulated as a fast finish/failure). The CP-2 controller releases the parent PG, requeues the trial, and replans — the trial completes with a single safe retry. Under FIFO the same scenario ends in FAILED because no retry logic exists.
scenarios.name: acc_cp2_node_loss_recovery

scenarios.description: Acceptance fixture (hash-frozen, NOT included in CP-1 totals): priority pre-emption under CP-2. A low-priority long-running job is running when a high-priority short job arrives. The CP-2 controller releases the low-priority job's parent PG and admits the high-priority job, then re-admits the low-priority job. Demonstrates that CP-2 can coordinate resource handoff. Under FIFO/greedy this coordination does not happen.
scenarios.name: acc_cp2_priority_preempt
